Fact.Name: Installment-sale Form 6252 entries
Fact.Description: One item represents one sale/disposition reported on a separate Form 6252.

Fact.Name: Installment sale is reported using the installment method
Fact.Description: Attest the sale is reportable on the installment method; dealer exclusions and elect-out determinations are resolved by the filer.

Fact.Name: Form 6252 line 1 property description
Fact.Description: Form 6252 line 1: the property code from the line 1 list, followed by a description of the installment sale property; both print together on line 1. Codes: 1 = timeshare or residential lot; 2 = sale by an individual of personal-use property (within the meaning of section 1275(b)(3)); 3 = sale of any property used or produced in the trade or business of farming (within the meaning of section 2032A(e)(4) or (5)); 4 = all other installment sales not listed.

Fact.Name: Form 6252 Line 21 current-year payments excluding interest
Fact.Description: Form 6252 line 21: all money and the fair market value of any property or services received during this tax year from the sale, excluding interest. An amount a prior year entered on the equivalent of line 34 (a deemed payment from a related party's second disposition) is not included here; it goes on line 23 with the prior-year payments, so the same gain is not taxed twice.

Fact.Name: Form 6252 note disposition choices
Fact.Description: The answers to "What happened to the buyer's note this year?", one per Form 6252 item. none, paidOffInFull, qualifyingSpouseTransfer and contributedToOwnEntity are not dispositions under IRC 453B and the item files. sold, settledForLess, gifted, cancelled, repossessed and other are refused by /knockoutForm6252InstallmentObligationDisposed.

Fact.Name: What happened to the buyer's note this year
Fact.Description: QUESTION: "What happened to the buyer's note (the installment obligation) this year?" Asked on every Form 6252 item. Answers: none - nothing: the buyer is still paying. Also choose this if you reduced the price without cancelling the rest of the debt, if a new buyer of the property took over the note, or if this is the final return of a seller who died holding the note. paidOffInFull - the buyer paid the whole balance, at full face value. sold - you sold or exchanged the note. settledForLess - you accepted less than the balance in full settlement, or took part payment and forgave the rest. gifted - you gave the note away. cancelled - you cancelled or forgave the note, or it became unenforceable. repossessed - you took the property back because the buyer did not pay. qualifyingSpouseTransfer - you transferred the note to your spouse, or to a former spouse because of a divorce; not to a trust, and your spouse or former spouse is not a nonresident alien. contributedToOwnEntity - you transferred the note, with no gain recognized, to a corporation for its stock under section 351, to a partnership for an interest under section 721, or to your own revocable trust; not to a life insurance company, or to a partnership with a life insurance company partner. other - anything else that disposed of the note. The first four and the last-but-one are not dispositions, and the item files as before. Every other answer is a disposition whose gain this return cannot figure yet, and /knockoutForm6252InstallmentObligationDisposed refuses it. Unanswered refuses nothing.

Fact.Name: This item's note was disposed of in a way this return cannot figure
Fact.Description: True when the item is reported on the installment method and "What happened to the buyer's note this year?" is answered sold, settledForLess, gifted, cancelled, repossessed or other. Those are IRC 453B dispositions (repossession has its own rules), whose gain or loss is the amount realized, or the note's fair market value, less the note's basis. That gain is not computed here. IsComplete first: an unanswered question, or an item not on the installment method, gives false.

Fact.Name: An installment note was disposed of this year
Fact.Description:
Blocks submission when any Form 6252 item has /form6252Sales/*/noteDispositionRefused true: the seller sold, settled for less, gave away, cancelled or otherwise disposed of the buyer's note this year, or repossessed the property. IRC 453B makes the remaining deferred gain taxable now, and Form 6252 has no line for it (the instructions send it to Form 4797, Form 8949 or Schedule D). This return cannot figure it yet, and asking the filer to figure it would be tax math outside the graph. IsComplete first over the sales collection: Complete false with no Form 6252.
SCREEN: "You said the buyer's note for one of your installment sales was sold, settled for less, given away, cancelled or otherwise disposed of this year, or that you repossessed the property. That makes the rest of the deferred gain taxable this year, and this return cannot figure that gain yet. You can't file this return here."

Fact.Name: The buyer's note was used as security for a loan
Fact.Description: QUESTION: "Have you used the buyer's note (the installment obligation) as security for a loan, this year or in an earlier year?" ASKED WHEN: the item is reported on the installment method and its line 5 selling price is above $150,000; below that the pledge rule cannot apply. Help text: a note is used as security to the extent the loan's principal or interest is directly secured by an interest in the note, including an arrangement that lets you pay off all or part of the loan with the note. Answer No when the property was personal-use property, property used or produced in farming, or a timeshare or residential lot, or when the loan only refinanced, without increasing its principal, a debt that was outstanding on December 17, 1987 and secured by the note since then. Validation: Boolean. UNANSWERED: refuses nothing. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../notePledgeRuleRefused and /knockoutForm6252PledgedInstallmentObligation. The net loan proceeds are a payment on the note, and later payments are not counted until they exceed them; this return does not figure that yet, so a Yes refuses the return.

Fact.Name: This item's note was pledged and the pledge rule applies
Fact.Description: True when the item is reported on the installment method, its line 5 selling price is above $150,000, its property is not answered as personal-use property on the line 26 reporting question, and the note is answered as used as security for a loan. Under IRC 453A(d) the net proceeds of such a loan are treated as a payment received on the note (limited to the contract price less the payments received before), and later payments are not taken into account until they exceed the amount so treated. Lines 21 and 23 would change by amounts this return does not ask for yet. IsComplete first: an unanswered question, an unanswered price, or an item not on the installment method gives false.

Fact.Name: An installment note subject to the pledge rule was used as security for a loan
Fact.Description:
Blocks submission when any Form 6252 item has /form6252Sales/*/notePledgeRuleRefused true: the note of a sale above $150,000 was used as security for a loan. IRC 453A(d) treats the net loan proceeds as a payment on the note and holds back later payments until they exceed that amount, and this return does not figure either yet. IsComplete first over the sales collection: Complete false with no Form 6252.
SCREEN: "You said the buyer's note for one of your installment sales was used as security for a loan. The loan proceeds count as a payment on the note, and this return cannot figure that yet. You can't file this return here."

Fact.Name: Form 6252 sale reporting destination options
Fact.Description: The six reporting destinations a gain or loss from this form can take: section1231 = property used in your trade or business (or held for the production of rents) held more than 1 year; ordinaryNoncapital = trade or business property held 1 year or less, or other property that is not a capital asset; capitalShortTerm / capitalLongTerm = a capital asset (investment property) held 1 year or less / more than 1 year; personalUseShortTerm / personalUseLongTerm = property held for personal use, such as your home, held 1 year or less / more than 1 year.

Fact.Name: Where this installment sale reports its Form 6252 line 26 (and line 37) gain
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "What kind of property did you sell on this installment sale, and how long did you hold it?" Options: section1231 = property used in your trade or business (or held for the production of rents) held more than 1 year; ordinaryNoncapital = trade or business property held 1 year or less, or other property that is not a capital asset; capitalShortTerm / capitalLongTerm = a capital asset (investment property) held 1 year or less / more than 1 year; personalUseShortTerm / personalUseLongTerm = property held for personal use, such as your home, held 1 year or less / more than 1 year. Help text: the Form 6252 instructions send line 26 (and line 37) to Form 4797 line 4 for trade or business property held more than 1 year, to Form 4797 line 10 for property held 1 year or less or an ordinary gain from a noncapital asset, and otherwise to Schedule D (line 4 short-term, line 11 long-term). A gain on personal-use property, such as your home, is a capital gain. ASKED WHEN: this sale files Form 6252 and its line 26 plus line 37 is above $0. UNANSWERED POSTURE: a positive amount with no answer leaves the Form 4797 and Schedule D lines it could feed Incomplete, so the return waits for the answer; a $0 amount never needs it. VALIDATION: one of the six options. WHAT IT FEEDS: form4797 /form6252Sales/*/form4797Line4Amount (section1231) and ../form4797Line10Amount (ordinaryNoncapital); scheduleD /form6252Sales/*/scheduleDShortTermAmount (capitalShortTerm, personalUseShortTerm) and ../scheduleDLongTermAmount (capitalLongTerm, personalUseLongTerm).
